entries.name: parseAddress
entries.doc:
Parses a free-form Pakistani address into structured components.

Extracts the postal code, matches known cities, districts and provinces
from the datasets, and assigns the remaining segments to {@link ParsedAddress.street}
and {@link ParsedAddress.area}. Works with or without commas between components.

entries.signature:

  String? raw,
  String? street,
  String? area,
  String? city,
  String? district,
  String? province,
  String? postalCode,
})
entries.doc:
Formats address components into a single mailing line, such as
`"House 12, Model Town, Lahore, Punjab 54000"`.

Only the components given are included; no postal code is invented.
{@link city} is used in preference to {@link district}. Returns {@link raw} (or `""`) when
no component is given. Pass the fields of a {@link ParsedAddress} to reformat
it.

entries.name: parseElectricityRef
entries.doc:
Parses a Pakistani electricity bill identifier: a DISCO reference number,
a DISCO customer ID or a K-Electric account number.

Formats are those the utilities' own bill pages ask for (retrieved
2026-11-18; see DATA.md in the repository): PITC's bill pages take a
14-digit reference number with a separate U/R choice, or a 10-digit
customer ID (11 digits for LESCO); K-Electric asks for a 13-digit account
number starting with `04000`. No check digit is published, so only the
format is checked.

Spaces, dashes and dots are ignored, and Urdu digits are accepted.

Returns `null` if the input matches none of the formats. Never throws.

```dart
parseElectricityRef('02-12624-0045901 R')?.formatted;
// '02 12624 0045901 R'
parseElectricityRef('0400012345678')?.disco; // 'K-Electric'
```

{@link parseElectricityRef}.


entries.name: validateCNIC
entries.doc:
Validates the format of a Pakistani CNIC number: 13 digits, in 5-7-1
groups or together, starting with a province code from 1 to 8.

Accepts `3520212345671`, `35202-1234567-1`, `35202 1234567 1` and Urdu
digits. Separators must sit between the 5-7-1 digit groups and be used
consistently.

NADRA does not publish a check-digit algorithm, so this validates
structure only.

entries.name: findCNICs
entries.doc:
Finds CNIC numbers in free text, such as a chat message, a note or an
uploaded document, for example to mask them before logging.

A match is 13 digits whose first digit is a province code (1-8), written
together or in 5-7-1 groups with a hyphen, dash, dot or space between the
groups (the two separators may differ). Digits may be ASCII, Urdu or
Arabic-Indic, even mixed. A match never starts or ends next to another
digit, so a longer number is not cut into a CNIC.

This is looser than {@link validateCNIC}, which needs the same separator
twice: text is written carelessly. It is a pattern match, so any other
13-digit number that starts with 1-8 (an account or order number, say)
also matches.

Offsets are UTF-16 code units, so `text.substring(m.start, m.end)` is
`m.raw`.

```dart
findCNICs('CNIC: 35202-1234567-1, phone 0300-1234567');
// [CNICMatch(raw: 35202-1234567-1, digits: 3520212345671,
//   formatted: 35202-1234567-1, start: 6, end: 21)]
```

Returns the matches in order, or an empty list. Never throws.

Courier helpers: courier statuses in one vocabulary, and city names as
couriers and customers write them. No courier API is called.

Same as the `pakdatakit/courier` entry point of the npm package.

fields.doc: The value used by the npm package, e.g. `"PostEx"`.

entries.name: CourierStatus
entries.doc:
A courier's status in one vocabulary, from order to delivery or return.

Experimental: the values may change in a minor release while more
couriers' status lists are added.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value used by the npm package, e.g. `"out-for-delivery"`.

values.name: pending
values.doc: Ordered, not yet booked with the courier.

values.name: returning
values.doc: On its way back to the sender.

entries.name: mapCourierStatus
entries.doc:
Maps a courier's own status (its name, numeric ID or code, as the courier
documents it) to a {@link CourierStatus}.

{@link courier} is `TCS`, `Leopards`, `PostEx`, `M&P`, `Trax` or `BlueEx`
(case-insensitive; `LCS`, `MnP` and `Blue Ex` are accepted), e.g.
{@link Courier.postEx}`.value`. {@link raw} is the status as the courier returned it:
a `String`, or a non-negative whole number (`int`, or a `double` such as
`5.0`), which matches the same status as its decimal string (`5` and
`'5'`, but not `'0005'`). Anything else gives `null`.

Matching ignores case and extra spaces. PostEx's `Attempt Made: <reason>`
history messages map to {@link CourierStatus.attempted}.

Only statuses the courier documents publicly are mapped: PostEx's API
guide and one Leopards status. TCS, M&P, Trax and BlueEx publish no list,
so they always return `null`, as does any status not in the list. No API
is called. Never throws.

Experimental: only PostEx and one Leopards status are mapped so far. The
mapping and the {@link CourierStatus} values may change in a minor release as
other couriers' lists are added.

entries.name: normalizeCityForCourier
entries.doc:
Maps the way a customer or a courier writes a city to the city's name in
pakdatakit's city list, so orders can be matched against a courier's
service list.

Accepts the exact name in any case, short forms (`LHR`, `Khi`, `Pindi`,
`Isb`, `FSD`), the old name Lyallpur, a trailing "city", and the main
cities in Urdu script.

```dart
normalizeCityForCourier('LHR');          // 'Lahore'
normalizeCityForCourier('lyallpur');     // 'Faisalabad'
normalizeCityForCourier('Karachi City'); // 'Karachi'
normalizeCityForCourier('Atlantis');     // null
```

Returns a city from the city list, or `null`. Never throws.

entries.name: expectedSalesTax
entries.doc:
The sales tax FBR expects on a line, in rupees, or `null` when the rate is
not a plain percentage or per-unit amount (spec §7, errors 0102, 0104,
0105):

- `N%` on Third Schedule goods: retail price × rate (0102);
- `N%` otherwise: value excluding sales tax × rate (0104);
- `Rs.N`: quantity × N (0105).

{@link item} is an {@link FbrInvoiceItem} (only `rate`, `saleType`, `quantity`,
`valueSalesExcludingST` and `fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice` are read).
Rounded half up to the paisa (the specification allows 2 decimals and
gives no rounding rule). Never throws.

```dart
expectedSalesTax({'rate': 'Rs.3', 'quantity': 12}); // 36
expectedSalesTax({'rate': '18%', 'valueSalesExcludingST': 1234}); // 222.12
```

entries.name: buildFbrInvoice
entries.doc:
Builds an FBR digital invoice from your own fields, working out
`salesTaxApplicable` on each line where you leave it out (see
{@link expectedSalesTax}; uses {@link calculateSalesTax}). Lines with a rate that is
neither `N%` nor `Rs.N` (`Exempt`, combined rates) get 0 unless you give
the tax.

{@link input} is an {@link FbrInvoiceInput} (a JSON map with an `items` list).
`salesTaxWithheldAtSource`, `totalValues` and
`fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice` default to 0, and `invoiceRefNo` and
`buyerNTNCNIC` to `""`, as in FBR's samples. Nothing else is filled in or
changed (other keys are kept); check the result with {@link validateFbrInvoice}.

Also returns column totals, which are for your own records: the
specification has no invoice-level totals.

Returns `null` if {@link input} is not a map with an `items` list of maps.
Never throws.

```dart
final built = buildFbrInvoice({
  'invoiceType': 'Sale Invoice',
  // … the other header fields …
  'items': [
    {'rate': '18%', 'quantity': 2, 'valueSalesExcludingST': 1234, /* … */},
  ],
})!;
(built.invoice['items']! as List).first['salesTaxApplicable']; // 222.12
built.totals.salesTaxApplicable; // 222.12
```

entries.name: validateFbrInvoice
entries.doc:
Checks an FBR digital invoice against the rules of PRAL's specification
(v1.12) and Error Message Guide that need no call to FBR, and returns every
problem with FBR's error code.

{@link invoice} is an [FbrInvoice]: a JSON map, e.g. from `jsonDecode` or
{@link buildFbrInvoice}. Anything else gives one error. Give {@link today}
(`YYYY-MM-DD`) to reject invoices dated later (error 0043); it is not
checked otherwise.

Checked: invoice type (0003, 0011), date format (0005, 0042, 0113) and,
with {@link today}, a future date (0043); seller and buyer NTN/CNIC (0401, 0402,
0009), self-invoicing (0058), names, provinces (0073, 0074), addresses,
buyer registration type (0012), the reference number of a debit note
(0026), the sandbox scenario, and on each line: HS code (0044), rate
(0020), unit, sale type (0013), required and valid amounts (0021, 0023,
0024, 0098, 0300, 0302), SRO schedule and serial (0077, 0078), Third
Schedule retail price (0090), extra tax on reduced-rate goods (0091) and
the sales tax arithmetic (0102, 0104, 0105, to within one paisa).

Not checked, because they need FBR's data: registration status, whether a
province, HS code, unit, rate, sale type or SRO is in FBR's lists or fits
the others, and the original invoice of a debit note.

Never throws.

```dart
validateFbrInvoice(invoice); // FbrInvoiceValidation{valid: true, errors: []}
validateFbrInvoice({...invoice, 'invoiceDate': '21-04-2025'}).errors.first;
// FbrInvoiceError{code: 0005, field: invoiceDate,
//   message: Invoice date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format}
```

Pakistani Rupee and lakh/crore formatting.

Same as the `pakdatakit/format` entry point of the npm package.

entries.name: formatPKR
entries.doc:
Formats an amount as Pakistani Rupees with comma separators, rounded to
whole rupees: `"Rs. 150,000"`. Negative amounts are prefixed with `-`
(`"-Rs. 500"`).

Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if {@link amount}
is NaN or infinite.

entries.name: formatLakh
entries.doc:
Formats an amount using Pakistani lakh/crore conventions.

- 1 crore or more renders as `"N Crore"` (`10000000` → `"1 Crore"`)
- 1 lakh or more renders as `"N Lakh"` (`2500000` → `"25 Lakh"`)
- smaller amounts fall back to {@link formatPKR}

Values are rounded to two decimals before the unit is chosen, so `9999999`
renders as `"1 Crore"` rather than `"100 Lakh"`. Negative amounts are
prefixed with `-`.

Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if {@link amount}
is NaN or infinite.

entries.name: parseAmount
entries.doc:
Reads a rupee amount the way people type it in Pakistan, and returns it in
rupees, rounded half-up to the paisa. Returns `null` for anything that is
not exactly one non-negative amount; it never throws.

Accepted:
- digits, with or without grouping: `150000`, `150,000` (international) or
  `1,50,000` (Pakistani: groups of two, then three), and decimals
  (`1,234.50`, `.5`, `5.`); a grouping must be complete and consistent;
- Urdu (`۱۵۰۰۰۰`) and Arabic-Indic (`١٥٠٠٠٠`) digits, also mixed with
  0-9, and the Arabic decimal and thousands separators (`٫`, `٬`);
- one currency mark before or after the number: `Rs`, `Rs.`, `PKR` or `₨`
  (any case), and a trailing `/-` (`Rs. 5,000/-`);
- one shorthand unit after the number, with or without a space, in any
  case: `k`, `thousand(s)`, `hazar`, `ہزار` (× 1,000); `lakh(s)`, `lac(s)`,
  `لاکھ` (× 100,000); `crore(s)`, `cr`, `کروڑ` (× 10,000,000). Decimals
  work with units: `1.5 lakh` is 150,000 and `2.25cr` is 22,500,000;
- whitespace around and between the parts (spaces, tabs, line breaks and
  no-break spaces).

Rejected (`null`): empty input, negative or signed amounts (`-500`,
`+500`), ranges (`5-10k`), more than one number (`500 600`), two currency
marks or two units, leftover letters (`500 rupees`, `5kk`), grouping that
could be read two ways or is broken (`1,50`, `1.500,00`, `1,5000`), and
amounts over Rs. 50 trillion (50 lakh crore), beyond which a number can no
longer hold every paisa exactly.

The arithmetic is done on the digits, so the result is exact: `1.005`
rounds to 1.01 and `1.5 lakh` is exactly 150000.

```dart
parseAmount('Rs. 1,50,000/-'); // ParsedAmount(value: 150000, raw: 'Rs. 1,50,000/-')
parseAmount('2.25cr');         // ParsedAmount(value: 22500000, raw: '2.25cr')
parseAmount('5-10k');          // null
```

entries.name: formatAmountInput
entries.doc:
Writes back an amount typed in any form {@link parseAmount} accepts, for
showing next to the field ("= Rs. 150,000"): `Rs.`, international
grouping, and paisa only when there are any (`Rs. 1,234.50`). Returns
`null` when {@link parseAmount} does; it never throws.

E.g. `"Rs. 150,000"` for `"1.5 lakh"`, or `null`.

The list is the 30 divisions of the 2023 census: Punjab 9, Sindh 6, Khyber
Pakhtunkhwa 7 and Balochistan 8. Islamabad has no division, and the census
tables do not cover Azad Jammu and Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. Divisions
created since the census (such as Gujrat in Punjab) are not included.

entries.name: getDivisionOfDistrict
entries.doc:
Returns the division a district belonged to in the 2023 census, or `null`
if not known. Matching is case-insensitive.

Census-district caveat: only the 136 districts of the 2023 census have a
division here, under the name they had then (so `Quetta`, `Dera Bugti` and
`South Waziristan` work, and their successors do not). Districts created
after the census, and those of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan and
Islamabad, return `null`.

entries.name: getTehsils
entries.doc:
Returns the tehsils (talukas, sub-divisions) of a district, sorted
alphabetically. Matching is case-insensitive; former district names such
as `Quetta` and `South Waziristan` work.

Census-district caveat: the data is the 591 tehsil-level units of the 2023
census, each recorded under the district it was in then. For a district of
the 2023 census this returns its census tehsils, even if some have since
moved to a new district (so `Rawalpindi` still lists Murree). For a
district created after the census it returns only the tehsils an official
source places in it, which can be an empty list. Azad Jammu and Kashmir
and Gilgit-Baltistan are not covered.

entries.name: getTehsilDistrict
entries.doc:
Returns the district a tehsil (taluka, sub-division) was in at the 2023
census, or `null`. Matching is case-insensitive.

Census-district caveat: the result is the census district, which may have
been split since (a tehsil of `Quetta` is now in Quetta East or Quetta
West). A few names are shared by tehsils in different districts (`Saddar`,
`Sahiwal`, `Khanpur`); pass the {@link province} to tell them apart. Returns
`null` when the name is unknown or still matches more than one district.

modules.name: package:pakdatakit/hijri.dart
modules.doc:
Hijri (Islamic) calendar conversion.

Same as the `pakdatakit/hijri` entry point of the npm package.

entries.doc: Islamic (Hijri) date components. See {@link toHijri}.

fields.doc: Hijri year (AH).

fields.name: month
fields.doc: Hijri month, 1 (Muharram) to 12 (Dhu al-Hijjah).

fields.name: day
fields.doc: Day of the month, 1–30.

methods.name: HijriDate
methods.signature: const HijriDate({required int year, required int month, required int day})
methods.doc: Creates a Hijri date. {@link month} is 1–12 and {@link day} 1–30.

methods.name: toJson
methods.doc: JSON form, with the same keys as the npm package.

entries.name: toHijri
entries.doc:
Converts a Gregorian date to a Hijri (Islamic) date.

Uses the tabular (arithmetic, "islamic-civil") calendar. Actual dates in
Pakistan follow moon sighting and can differ by a day or two; pass
{@link offset} (whole days, e.g. `-1` when Pakistan's Ruet-e-Hilal calendar runs
a day behind the tabular date) to adjust. The local calendar date of
{@link date} is used; the time of day is ignored.

entries.name: fromHijri
entries.doc:
Converts a Hijri date to a Gregorian date (local midnight).

Use the same {@link offset} as with {@link toHijri}. Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a
`RangeError` in the npm package) if the components are out of range
(year below 1, month outside 1–12 or day outside 1–30).

entries.name: formatHijri
entries.doc:
Formats a Gregorian date as a Hijri date string, e.g. `"14 Ramadan 1447"`.
See {@link toHijri} for {@link offset}.

entries.name: getHijriMonthName
entries.doc:
Returns the English name of a Hijri month (1–12), or `null` if {@link month} is
out of range.

entries.name: isRamadan
entries.doc:
Whether a Gregorian date falls in the month of Ramadan. See {@link toHijri} for
{@link offset}.

methods.doc:

entries.name: getPakistanHolidays
entries.doc:
Lists Pakistan's federal public holidays for a {@link year}, sorted by date.

Islamic holidays use the dates actually observed after moon sighting
(2020 onwards, from Cabinet Division and SBP notifications). For years not
yet in the dataset they are estimated from the tabular Hijri calendar and
marked {@link Holiday.estimated}; pass {@link announced} to use official dates
instead.

- [includeChristianHolidays]: include 26 December, a holiday for
  Christian employees only.
- [announced]: observed or announced dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for Islamic
  holidays, used instead of the dataset or estimate. An empty list removes
  that holiday for the year. Entries for non-Islamic holidays are ignored.
- [hijriOffset]: day offset applied to estimated Islamic dates.

Optional holidays (e.g. Shab-e-Barat, Easter, Youm-e-Ali) are not
included. Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if
{@link year} is not from 1948 to 9999 or an announced date is not `YYYY-MM-DD`.

entries.name: getHolidaysOn

calendar date) or a `YYYY-MM-DD` {@link String}. Empty if it is not a public
holiday.

Takes the same options as {@link getPakistanHolidays}. Throws an
{@link ArgumentError} for any other kind of value or a malformed string.

entries.name: isPakistanHoliday
entries.doc:
Whether a date is a Pakistani federal public holiday. See
{@link getHolidaysOn}.

Tax for the year from the rate table, in rupees, rounded half up to the
paisa.

The section 4AB surcharge, rounded half up to the paisa. `0` unless
`includeSurcharge` is set and the year and income attract one.

methods.doc: JSON form, with the same keys as the npm package.

entries.name: getTaxYear
entries.doc:
The tax year (July to June) that contains {@link date}, or `null` for an
invalid date.

{@link date} is a `YYYY-MM-DD` {@link String} or a {@link DateTime} (its local calendar
date), and defaults to today. A tax year is named after the June it ends
in. Never throws.

```dart
getTaxYear('2025-06-30'); // 2025
getTaxYear('2025-07-01'); // 2026
```

entries.name: getSalaryTaxSlabs
entries.doc:
Returns the salaried rate table for a tax year: Division I of Part I of
the First Schedule to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, clause (2), which
applies when salary is more than 75% of taxable income.

Covers tax years 2020 to 2027, each from FBR's consolidated Ordinance.
{@link taxYear} is e.g. `2026` (1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026) and defaults to the
current tax year.

Returns `null` for a year that is not covered. Never throws.

entries.name: getSalaryTaxYears
entries.doc: Which tax years {@link getSalaryTaxSlabs} covers, oldest first.

entries.name: calculateSalaryTax
calculateMonthlySalaryTax
entries.doc:
{@link calculateSalaryTax} for a monthly salary: the income is
`monthlySalary × 12`, and {@link SalaryTax.monthly} is the tax to withhold each
month. {@link includeSurcharge} adds the section 4AB surcharge, as in
{@link calculateSalaryTax}. Never throws.

```dart
calculateMonthlySalaryTax(150000, taxYear: 2026)?.monthly; // 6000
```

values.name: invalid
values.doc: Cannot become valid by typing more (wrong character, prefix or length).

entries.name: formatCNICInput
entries.doc:
Formats a CNIC as the user types: `35202-1234567-1`.

Keeps up to 13 digits (Urdu digits are converted) and inserts the dashes
as the groups fill. Other characters are dropped.

entries.name: checkCNICInput
entries.doc:
Checks a CNIC while the user is typing.

```dart
checkCNICInput('35202-12');        // InputState.incomplete
checkCNICInput('35202-1234567-1'); // InputState.valid
checkCNICInput('05202');           // InputState.invalid
```

entries.doc:
Formats a Pakistani mobile number as the user types: `0300-1234567`, or
`+92 300 1234567` when the user starts with the country code.

entries.name: checkPhoneInput
entries.doc:
Checks a Pakistani mobile number while the user is typing. The `03XX`
prefix is checked as soon as it is complete.

```dart
checkPhoneInput('0300 12');     // InputState.incomplete
checkPhoneInput('0360');        // InputState.invalid (not allocated)
checkPhoneInput('03001234567'); // InputState.valid
```

entries.doc:
Formats an IBAN as the user types: uppercase, in groups of four
(`PK36 SCBL 0000 0011 2345 6702`), up to 24 characters.

entries.name: checkIBANInput
entries.doc:
Checks a Pakistani IBAN while the user is typing: the `PK` prefix, check
digits and bank code are checked as they are typed, and the full checksum
once all 24 characters are in.

```dart
checkIBANInput('PK36 SC');                       // InputState.incomplete
checkIBANInput('GB29');                          // InputState.invalid
checkIBANInput('PK36 SCBL 0000 0011 2345 6702'); // InputState.valid
```

entries.name: scoreAddress
entries.doc:
Scores how complete a free-form Pakistani delivery address is, for cash on
delivery and other courier use.

Built on {@link parseAddress}. It looks for a city, a house, plot or flat
number, a street, an area, a postal code and a landmark ("near", "opp",
"nazd", "qareeb", "سامنے" …), and adds up {@link addressWeights}. A postal code
that is a known post office raises the score more than an unknown one,
and a post office in a different province from the city lowers it (with a
warning in {@link ParsedAddress.warnings}).

This is a heuristic: it says how much an address tells a rider, not
whether the address exists. It never throws.

```dart

    'near Liberty Market, Lahore 54660').score; // 100
```

entries.name: createRaastP2PQr
entries.signature:
String createRaastP2PQr({
  required String iban,
  String? scheme,
  num? amount,
  DateTime? expiresAt,
  Object? expiresIn,
  String? bankName,
  String? particulars,
  DateTime? now,
})
entries.doc:
Creates a Raast person-to-person QR payload in SBP's P2P QR format
(payload format `02`), matching the QR codes banking apps generate, so it
can be scanned by apps such as Easypaisa and JazzCash. Encode the string as
a QR code with any QR library.

- [iban]: payee's Pakistani IBAN.
- [scheme]: scheme identifier (tag 02), `'00'` (default, as used by
  banking apps) or `'30'` (the value listed for Raast in SBP's standard).
- [amount]: amount in PKR. When set, the QR is dynamic (point of
  initiation 12) and an expiry is required: banking apps reject dynamic QR
  codes without one, and ignore the amount in static ones.
- [expiresAt]: when a QR with an amount stops working (tag 07).
- [expiresIn]: instead of {@link expiresAt}, how long from {@link now} a QR with an
  amount works: a {@link Duration}, milliseconds, or a string such as `'30m'`,
  `'12h'` or `'7d'`.
- [bankName]: payee's bank name (up to 25 characters).
- [particulars]: payment description (up to 30 characters).
- [now]: the time {@link expiresIn} counts from. Defaults to {@link DateTime.now}.

```dart
createRaastP2PQr(iban: 'PK36SCBL0000001123456702');
createRaastP2PQr(
    iban: 'PK36SCBL0000001123456702', amount: 1500, expiresIn: '1d');
```

Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if the IBAN
is invalid, a field is too long, or an amount is given without
{@link expiresAt} or {@link expiresIn}.

entries.name: createMerchantQr
entries.signature:
String createMerchantQr({
  required MerchantAccountInfo merchantAccount,
  required String merchantName,
  required String city,
  String? mcc,
  num? amount,
  bool? isDynamic,
  String? billNumber,
  String? mobileNumber,
  String? reference,
  DateTime? dueDate,
  num? amountAfterDueDate,
})
entries.doc:
Creates an EMVCo merchant-presented QR payload following SBP's Pakistan
QR standard (currency `586`, country `PK`, CRC in tag 63), including the
Pakistan-specific due-date fields.

SBP leaves the layout of the Raast merchant account template to the
scheme and has shared it only with banks, so pass the template sub-fields
your bank gives you in {@link merchantAccount}.

- [merchantName]: up to 25 characters. [city]: up to 15 characters.
- [mcc]: ISO 18245 merchant category code. Defaults to `0000`.
- [amount]: amount in PKR. When set, the QR is dynamic unless
  {@link isDynamic} is `false`.
- [isDynamic]: overrides the point of initiation (static `11` / dynamic
  `12`); `dynamic` in the npm package.
- {@link billNumber} (tag 62-01, up to 25 characters), {@link mobileNumber} (62-02, up
  to 15) and {@link reference} (62-05, up to 25).
- {@link dueDate} (Pakistan-specific tag 62-50) and {@link amountAfterDueDate}
  (62-51), which must be used together.

Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if a field
is missing, too long, or out of range.

entries.name: parseRaastQr
entries.doc:
Parses a Raast QR payload: either a person-to-person QR (payload format
`02`) or an EMVCo merchant QR (payload format `01`), and verifies its CRC.

Returns `null` if the payload is not a well-formed Pakistani QR code.

entries.name: validateRaastQr
entries.doc:
Checks whether a Raast QR code can be paid, e.g. before showing a payment
screen or to warn about a tampered sticker.

Errors: not a Pakistani payment QR, checksum mismatch (damaged or edited),
a person-to-person QR with no IBAN, an IBAN that fails its checksum,
expired, or a fixed-amount QR without the expiry that banking apps
require.

Warnings: an amount in a static QR (apps ignore it, so the payer must
type it), a QR that expires within {@link expiresSoonMs} milliseconds (an hour
by default) of {@link now} (defaults to {@link DateTime.now}), or a merchant QR with
no IBAN ({@link RaastQrWarning.noIban}): merchant QRs may pay through the
merchant's own scheme, so it is valid, but the payee can't be checked
from the QR.

The result's `kind` says whether the QR is person-to-person or a
merchant QR (`null` when it is not a Raast QR).

```dart
validateRaastQr(scannedText);
// valid: false, kind: p2p, errors: [expired], warnings: [], qr: ...
```

entries.name: getSalesTaxRate
entries.doc:
Returns the standard sales tax rate for goods (federal, Sales Tax Act
1990) or for services in a province or Islamabad Capital Territory, on a
given date.

{@link province} accepts the province names and `KP`, `KPK`, `ICT` and
`Islamabad`; for goods it may be left out. {@link date} is a `YYYY-MM-DD`
{@link String} or a {@link DateTime} (its local calendar date), and defaults to today.

Only standard rates are covered, from 1 July 2019. Reduced, higher and
sector rates are not.

Returns `null` for an unknown province, services without a province,
goods in Azad Jammu and Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan, an invalid date, or a
date before 1 July 2019. Never throws.

```dart
getSalesTaxRate(kind: SalesTaxKind.goods, date: '2026-11-18')?.rate; // 18
getSalesTaxRate(
    kind: SalesTaxKind.services, province: 'Sindh', date: '2024-06-30')
  ?.rate; // 13
```

entries.name: splitInclusive
calculateSalesTax
entries.signature:
SalesTaxAmounts? calculateSalesTax(
  num amount, {
  num? rate,
  String? province,
  SalesTaxKind? kind,
  Object? date,
  bool inclusive = false,
})
entries.doc:
Adds sales tax to {@link amount} (0 to 1 trillion rupees), or splits it out
when {@link inclusive} is `true`.

Give a {@link rate} (percent, 0 to 100, at most 2 decimals), or a {@link province}
(and {@link kind}, default {@link SalesTaxKind.services} when a province is given,
and {@link date}) to use the standard rate from {@link getSalesTaxRate}. {@link rate} takes
precedence over {@link province}. The tax is rounded half up to the paisa.

Returns `null` if the amount, rate or province is invalid or no rate
applies. Never throws.

```dart
calculateSalesTax(1000, rate: 18);
// SalesTaxAmounts{net: 1000.0, tax: 180.0, gross: 1180.0, rate: 18.0}
calculateSalesTax(1000, province: 'Punjab', date: '2026-11-18')?.tax; // 160
calculateSalesTax(1150,
    province: 'Sindh', date: '2026-11-18', inclusive: true)?.net; // 1000
```

alphabetical order and bidirectional text.

Same as the `pakdatakit/text` entry point of the npm package.

`nhi` → `nahi`).

Also applies {@link normalizeText} and converts Urdu/Arabic digits to English.
A capitalized word keeps its capital; all-caps words (acronyms such as
"AP") are left unchanged.

entries.doc: Converts English and Arabic-Indic digits to Urdu digits (۰–۹).

{@link latin} (a-z only) or {@link urdu} (Urdu letters only).

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value used by the npm package, e.g. `"latin"`.

entries.name: slugify
entries.doc:
Turns text into a URL slug: lower-case words joined by `-`.

Urdu letters are kept as they are (no transliteration: Urdu does not write
short vowels, so there is no single Roman spelling). Diacritics, tatweel
and zero-width characters are dropped, the Arabic look-alikes ك ي ى become
the Urdu ک ی ی, Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits become `0-9`, and accented
Latin-1 letters lose their accents (`é` → `e`, `ß` → `ss`). Anything else
separates words. {@link script} limits which letters are kept; digits are always
kept, as `0-9`.

Returns `''` when nothing is left. Never throws.

```dart
slugify('Lahore Fort, 2024'); // 'lahore-fort-2024'
slugify('لاہور قلعہ'); // 'لاہور-قلعہ'
slugify('لاہور Fort', script: SlugScript.latin); // 'fort'
slugify('کراچی ۲۰۲۴', script: SlugScript.urdu); // 'کراچی-2024'
```

entries.name: compareUrdu
entries.doc:
Compares two strings in Urdu alphabetical order, for {@link List.sort}.

Letters follow the Unicode CLDR collation for Urdu (`ur`, CLDR 49):
ا آ ب بھ پ پھ ت تھ ٹ ٹھ ث ج جھ چ چھ ح خ د دھ ڈ ڈھ ذ ر رھ ڑ ڑھ ز ژ س ش ص ض
ط ظ ع غ ف ق ک کھ گ گھ ل لھ م مھ ن نھ ں ںھ و وھ ہ ھ ۃ ء ی یھ ے. A letter
joined with ھ is a letter of its own (so بھ comes after every other ب
word). أ ؤ ۂ ئ ۓ sort as ا و ہ ی ے and come just after them when words
are otherwise equal, and diacritics only break ties, in CLDR's order.

Outside the Urdu letters: spaces and punctuation come first, then digits
digit by digit (Urdu, Arabic-Indic and ASCII digits are equal; `10` comes
before `2`), then Urdu letters, then other Arabic-script characters (the
look-alikes ك ي ى ه ة, which CLDR does not treat as Urdu letters), then
everything else by code point, ignoring ASCII case. Strings that are
still equal are ordered by code point, so the result is 0 only for
identical strings. The order is the same on every platform; ICU is not
used.

Returns `-1`, `0` or `1`. Never throws.

```dart
['ے', 'بھائی', 'آم', 'باغ', 'اب']..sort(compareUrdu);
// ['اب', 'آم', 'باغ', 'بھائی', 'ے']
```

entries.name: isRTL
entries.doc:
Whether text reads right to left: its first letter is from a right-to-left
script such as Urdu or Arabic. Digits, punctuation and spaces are skipped,
as in the Unicode bidirectional algorithm's paragraph rule.

Returns `false` when there is no letter. Never throws.

```dart
isRTL('سلام'); // true
isRTL('123 سلام'); // true
isRTL('Order نمبر'); // false
```

entries.name: BidiDirection
entries.doc:
Direction for [wrapBidi]: {@link auto} follows the first strong letter, {@link rtl}
and {@link ltr} force right-to-left or left-to-right.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value used by the npm package, e.g. `"rtl"`.

values.name: auto
values.doc: FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068): the direction of the first letter.

entries.name: wrapBidi
entries.doc:
Wraps text in Unicode directional isolates, so a name or number in one
direction does not reorder the sentence around it (for example an English
order number inside an Urdu message).

Uses FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068) by default, RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE
(U+2067) for {@link BidiDirection.rtl} and LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE (U+2066) for
{@link BidiDirection.ltr}, closed with POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE (U+2069). Never
throws.

```dart
'آرڈر ${wrapBidi('PDK-1042')} بھیج دیا گیا';
```

entries.name: romanUrduKey
entries.doc:
A phonetic key for Roman Urdu, so that different spellings of the same
name or word match: `Mubeen` and `Mobeen`, `Muhammad`, `Mohammad` and
`Muhammed`, `Rehman` and `Rahman`, `Chaudhry`, `Chaudhary` and
`Chaudhery`. Compare keys, not the text.

Each word keeps its consonants, its first vowel sound and a vowel sound
at its end. Letters for one sound are merged (`kh`, `sh`, `ch`; `ph` and
`f`; `q`, `c` and `k`; `v` and `w`; `th` and `t`, `dh` and `d`), doubled
letters count once, `e` counts as `a`, `o` as `u`, and a final `h` after
a vowel is dropped. Accents are removed and anything other than Latin
letters splits words. The key is not meant to be shown: it is an opaque
string.

Different names can share a key (`Hamid` and `Hamad`), so treat a match
as "probably the same", not proof. {@link normalizeRomanUrdu} is a different
tool: it rewrites informal spellings into readable text.

```dart
romanUrduKey('Mubeen') == romanUrduKey('Mobeen'); // true
romanUrduKey('Muhammad Rehman'); // 'muhmd rahmn'
romanUrduKey('Hussain') == romanUrduKey('Hassan'); // false
```

Returns the key, one part per word separated by spaces, or `''` for text
with no Latin letters. Never throws.

There is no single national format, so this accepts the common shape: 1–4
letters, then 1–4 digits, optionally followed by a two-digit year after a
separator (`LEA-1234-19`). Series letters are not checked. Returns `null`
if the plate does not have that shape. See DATA.md in the repository.

entries.name: numberToWords
entries.doc:
Converts a whole number to words using the Pakistani numbering system
(hundred, thousand, lakh, crore, arab, kharab).

```dart
numberToWords(125000); // 'one lakh twenty-five thousand'
numberToWords(125000, language: WordsLanguage.ur); // 'ایک لاکھ پچیس ہزار'
```

Throws an {@link ArgumentError} (a `RangeError` in the npm package) if {@link n} is
not a safe integer (a whole number within ±(2^53 − 1)).
